Inductive effect The electron cloud in a sigma bond (o) between two unlike atoms in not uniform. It is more dense towards the more electronegative of the two atoms i.e. the electron pair forming the sigma bond is slightly displaced towards X, this permanent state of polarization is called the inductive effect. It is represented by arrow ( s The atom X thus acquires a slight negative charge (ö—) and the carbon atom a slight positive charge ((5+) i.e. the bond is polarized. If the electronegative atom is joined to a chain of carbon atoms, the positive charge on the carbon atom is related to the other carbon atoms.
Depending upon the nature of groups attached to the carbon chain, there are two types of inductive effect.

Positive inductive effect or + I effect : If the group attached to carbon atom tn the carbon chain is less electronegative than carbon, the carbon atom gets partial negative charge and group gets partial positive charge because the bonding electrons are displaced towards carbon atom. Such inductive effect is known as positive inductive effect. Examples: -CH3, -COO¯, -CH2R,-CR3 etc.
